channel.title: EngineerzCorneR — Posts
channel.description: Deep-dive technical write-ups across Electrical, Mechanical, HVAC, Automation, Civil and Solar.

item.title: AWG vs mm²: Converting Wire Gauge to Metric Cross-Section
item.description: How AWG is defined, the doubling rules of thumb, common AWG sizes in mm2, and why matching area does not replace an ampacity check.

item.title: Cable Schedules Explained: What Goes in One and How It Drives Ordering and Handover
item.description: The fields in a cable schedule, how to choose cable type, a worked example turning a schedule into an order quantity, and what a schedule does not check.

item.title: Compressed Air Systems: Where the Energy Goes and How to Cut It
item.description: Why compressed air is costly, how leaks and excess pressure waste energy, with worked cost examples, receiver sizing and habits that cut the bill.

item.title: Concrete Grades Explained: What C25/30 Means and Why the Water-Cement Ratio Matters
item.description: How to read concrete grades such as C25/30, how cylinder and cube strength differ, and why the water-cement ratio controls strength.

item.title: Corrosion and Cathodic Protection Basics: Why Steel Rusts and How Coatings and Anodes Stop It
item.description: A visual guide to the corrosion cell, a worked corrosion rate example, galvanic potentials and cathodic protection with anodes or impressed current.

item.title: Earth Fault Loop Impedance Explained: Why the Breaker Must Trip Fast Enough
item.description: What earth fault loop impedance is, disconnection times, maximum Zs for MCB types, the 0.8 rule, cable length limits and TT systems.

item.title: Fan Static vs Total Pressure: What the Fan Is Really Working Against
item.description: How static, velocity and total pressure relate, and how to work out fan total and static pressure from field readings, with worked examples.

item.title: Fire Alarm Systems Explained: Detection, Circuits and Standby Power

item.title: Heat Recovery Ventilation: HRV, ERV and What Effectiveness Really Means

item.title: Piping Pressure Tests Explained: Hydrostatic and Pneumatic Leak Testing to ASME B31.3
item.description: How ASME B31.3 sets hydrostatic and pneumatic test pressures, the stress ratio, a worked example, hold time and practical test hazards.

item.title: Incoterms 2020 Explained: Who Pays, and Where the Risk Passes

item.title: Infrared Thermography for Electrical Inspection: Finding Hot Spots Before They Fail

item.title: From Instrument Index to I/O List: Counting Points and Sizing Cards

item.title: IP and IK Ratings Explained: Reading the Codes on Enclosures

item.title: Maximum Demand, Demand Factor and Diversity: Sizing a Supply Below the Connected Load

item.title: Motor Efficiency Classes Explained: IE1 to IE4, the EU Rules and What the Savings Look Like
item.description: What IE1 to IE4 motor efficiency classes mean, the EU Ecodesign dates, a worked running cost comparison and why sizing and speed control matter.

item.title: Motor Overload Protection: How Overload Relays and Trip Classes Work

item.title: Pipe Insulation Thickness and Heat Loss: Why Each Layer Helps Less

item.title: Pipe Wall Thickness (ASME B31.3)

item.title: Protective Coating Systems Explained: Reading the Aramco APCS Table in Pictures
item.description: A visual guide to Aramco APCS coating systems: layers, the 1A to 1F decoder, temperature ladder, thickness chart, blast grades and selection.

item.title: Pump Power Explained: From Hydraulic Power to Shaft Power to Motor Size

item.title: RCD, RCCB and RCBO Explained: How Residual Current Protection Works and Which Type to Use

item.title: RFIs and the RFI Log: Raising, Tracking and Closing Requests for Information

item.title: SEER, EER and COP Explained: Reading Cooling Efficiency Ratings Correctly

item.title: Shaft Diameter Sizing: Combining Bending and Torsion with the ASME Equation

item.title: Solar CO2 Offset: How Avoided Emissions Are Estimated, and Why the Factor Matters
item.description: How to estimate CO2 avoided by solar, average vs marginal grid factors, lifecycle emissions, degradation and how reliable tree and car equivalents are.

item.title: Solar Shading and Soiling Losses: Why Small Obstructions Cost More Than Their Size
item.description: Why a small shadow cuts output more than its area, how bypass diodes limit the damage, typical soiling losses, and how to decide whether panel cleaning pays.

item.title: Steam Traps Explained: Types, Failure Modes and What a Leaking Trap Costs
item.description: How steam traps work, the three families with diagrams, how they fail, what a leaking trap costs and how often to test them.
